continuity.compare_external_anchors#7: 0600:783, the default of v_anchor_level `coalesce(bool_or(p.chain_key is null), false)` becomes `true`. The two differ only when bool_or returns NULL. Its argument `p.chain_key is null` is never NULL, so that happens only when continuity.external_anchor_problems(a) returns no row. With no row, v_problems is coalesce(array_agg(...), '{}') = '{}', so the status CASE takes its first branch (`cardinality(v_problems) = 0`, MATCH) and never reads v_anchor_level. v_anchor_level is a local, set again for every anchor by the same one-row aggregate SELECT INTO, and it is not an output column. No input changes any returned row.
continuity.compare_external_anchors#13: 0600:795, `coalesce(pg_input_is_valid(h ->> 'seq', 'bigint'), false)` in the v_lost aggregate becomes `true`. pg_input_is_valid is STRICT and its second argument is a constant, so the two differ only for a head whose h ->> 'seq' is NULL (key absent, JSON null, or the head is not an object). Such a head has a NULL Merkle leaf in kernel.merkle_root (0010: sha256(convert_to(chain_key || ':' || seq || ':' || hash_hex)) is NULL when seq is NULL). A NULL leaf makes the computed root NULL: every level either carries a node up unchanged or replaces it by sha256(x || y), which is NULL when either side is, down to one node. continuity.external_anchor_problems compares that root with `is distinct from` (the DEFECT fix of this review: with `<>` a NULL root was never reported), and v_root is not NULL there (a NULL v_root returns 'malformed' first), so it reports 'root does not match its heads' with chain_key NULL. v_anchor_level is then true and the DISCARDABLE WHEN is false whatever v_lost is; the status is UNEXPLAINED in both. v_lost is a local, not an output column. The test 'lost history is discardable only when every differing head has a readable position...' holds this case (a head without seq next to a lost head: UNEXPLAINED).
continuity.compare_external_anchors#19: 0600:798, the default of v_lost `coalesce(bool_and(...), false)` becomes `true` (the CASE's own `else false` is #18, killed). bool_and returns NULL only over zero rows, because each input `case when <seq is a valid bigint> then (h ->> 'seq')::bigint > coalesce((select last_seq ...), 0) else false end` is never NULL: a valid bigint text casts to a non-NULL value, the right side is coalesced, the ELSE is false. Zero rows means no element of a -> 'heads' has its chain_key in v_chains. If v_chains is empty, the DISCARDABLE WHEN is already false through `cardinality(v_chains) > 0`. If v_chains is not empty, each key in it came from a row that continuity.external_anchor_problems emitted inside its loop over the same array (p_anchor -> 'heads', reached only when jsonb_typeof is 'array', the same test this query applies) with chain_key := h ->> 'chain_key', the expression this query filters on; that head is therefore a row and bool_and is not NULL. v_lost is a local, not an output column.
continuity.compare_external_anchors#25: 0600:803, `when coalesce(pg_input_is_valid(a ->> 'created_at', 'timestamptz'), false) then (a ->> 'created_at')::timestamptz > p_restore_point else false end` becomes `coalesce(..., true)`. pg_input_is_valid is STRICT and its second argument is a constant, so it returns NULL only when a ->> 'created_at' is NULL (key absent, JSON null, or the element is not an object). Then the mutant evaluates NULL::timestamptz > p_restore_point, which is NULL, where the original gives false. v_after_point is read only as one conjunct of the DISCARDABLE WHEN of the status CASE: a NULL conjunct makes that AND NULL or false, never true, and a WHEN whose condition is NULL is not taken, exactly as for false, so the status is UNEXPLAINED in both. The reachable neighbours are killed by the kill test: an anchor created exactly at the restore point and one whose creation time is not a time are UNEXPLAINED (#27, #28).
continuity.compare_external_anchors#39: 0600:809, `cardinality(v_chains) > 0` becomes `>= 0` in the DISCARDABLE WHEN. v_chains is coalesced to '{}', so `>= 0` is always true, and the two differ only when v_chains is empty. That WHEN is evaluated only after `cardinality(v_problems) = 0` was false, so continuity.external_anchor_problems returned at least one row. With v_chains empty every such row has chain_key NULL (v_chains aggregates every non-NULL chain_key), so v_anchor_level = bool_or(true) = true and the conjunct `not v_anchor_level` is false. Independently, v_lost is coalesce(bool_and over no rows, false) = false, since no head has a chain_key in an empty array. The WHEN is false with either operator and the status is UNEXPLAINED. The conjunct is redundant, not wrong, and is kept (a guard is never removed to silence a mutant).
continuity.verify_external_anchors#20: 0600:1236, the filter `coalesce(pg_input_is_valid(h ->> 'seq', 'bigint'), false)` of `select min((h ->> 'seq')::bigint) into v_seq` becomes `coalesce(..., true)`. pg_input_is_valid is STRICT and its second argument is a constant, so the mutant admits exactly the extra heads whose h ->> 'seq' is NULL. For those, (h ->> 'seq')::bigint is NULL (casting NULL raises nothing) and min() ignores NULL inputs, so min is taken over the same non-NULL values: v_seq is identical (NULL when there is none). The aggregate always returns one row, and nothing else reads the filter.
esig.check_witness#22: This is a clock boundary: `v_act_at > clock_timestamp()` becomes `>=`. The two differ only when the stored act time equals, to the microsecond, the value clock_timestamp() returns inside this comparison. clock_timestamp() is the server wall clock read at evaluation. No caller or role can set or freeze it: search_path pins pg_catalog first, so it cannot be shadowed. The act time is fixed before the call. So no input, stored state or call sequence can produce the equal case deterministically. Any attempt is decided by microsecond timing, not by what the test controls. At the boundary the original accepts an act recorded exactly 'now', which is not in the future, and that is the correct reading.
esig.check_witness#2: The mutant turns `v_act is null OR jsonb_typeof(v_act) <> 'object' OR coalesce(v_act->>'device_id','')='' OR coalesce(v_act->>'at','')=''` into `(v_act is null AND jsonb_typeof(v_act) <> 'object') OR C OR D`, because AND binds tighter than OR. Whenever the first or the second term is true, v_act is SQL NULL or a non-object jsonb (null, string, number, boolean or array). For every one of those, the text-field operator `->> 'device_id'` returns NULL without raising, so term C, `coalesce(...,'') = ''`, is already true and ESIG-050 is still raised. When both terms are false, the change makes no difference. None of the terms has a side effect or can raise. The result is identical for every value of p_provided.
esig.check_witness#24: This is a clock boundary: `clock_timestamp() - v_act_at > v_window` becomes `>=`. The two differ only when the elapsed time equals the witness window (300 s by default) exactly to the microsecond, measured against the clock_timestamp() read inside the comparison. As for check_witness#22, that reading cannot be set, frozen or predicted by any input, state or call sequence, so the difference cannot be observed deterministically. At the boundary the original keeps the window inclusive: an act exactly one window old is 'within the witness window', which is correct.
esig.content_changed#10:
With the mutant (0220:309, `v_computed := true` becomes false) the hash `esig.content_hash_of(type, id, esig.provide(type, id))` is recomputed on every loop iteration instead of once per call. Results can differ only if that expression returns different values between two iterations of one call.
(1) content_hash_of is immutable over the provider output, and the provider contract in 0200 forbids a provider from changing data. A non-deterministic provider could never be signed: the hash at the challenge would differ from the hash at signing (EBMR-ESIG-012), so there would be no signature for the loop to visit.
(2) The only writes between iterations are the esig.signature_invalidation row (its stamp trigger and audit trigger) and the kernel.audit_business_event entry (a kernel.audit_event row, action BUSINESS or table esig.signature_invalidation). No trigger on those tables touches a signed table, and no registered provider's hashed fields (content, content_version) read them:
- esig_stub reads only esig.stub_signable.
- sample_record counts only audit events with table_name 'platform.stub_record' and action 'UPDATE'.
- The records and continuity providers have no signed tables. content_changed is owner-private (no grant; migration 0220 comment at line 489), so it runs only from esig.on_signed_content_change and never for those types.
(3) A concurrent commit cannot change hashed content between iterations. content_changed holds the aggregate's transaction-scoped advisory lock (esig.aggregate_lock) until commit, and every other change to that aggregate's hashed content goes through the same trigger, which waits on the same lock before its transaction can commit. For sample_record the changed row's row lock is also held. Only a superuser disabling triggers (session_replication_role = replica) could interleave a change; that is outside the trust boundary and is detected separately by esig.verify_signatures and the INV-09 invariant.
The only difference left is the number of provider calls, which is performance and not behaviour. Checked with a per-mutant run of all 7 new tests plus the group's existing tests: none detects it.
esig.sign#14: This is a clock boundary: `clock_timestamp() > v_ch.expires_at` becomes `>=`. The two differ only when the clock_timestamp() read inside the comparison equals the stored expires_at to the microsecond. Time travel can move expires_at to any value, but not to the unknown clock reading taken later inside esig.sign. The clock cannot be frozen or shadowed (pg_catalog is first on the pinned search_path). No input, state or call sequence can observe the difference deterministically. The existing test covers both sides away from the instant: an expired challenge is refused (ESIG-033), a fresh one is accepted.

Both sides near the limit are tested (accepted just inside, refused just outside). Same class as esig.sign#14 and esig.check_witness#18/#20.

kernel.current_actor#1: The body is `select case when kernel.actor_context_validated() then current_setting('ebmr.ctx', true)::jsonb end`. The mutant only changes missing_ok (true to false) in the THEN branch. That branch runs only after actor_context_validated() has returned true, which needs coalesce(current_setting('ebmr.ctx', true), '') <> ''. So the setting exists and is non-empty at that moment. Nothing between the WHEN and the THEN can change or remove it: it is the same expression evaluation, and actor_context_validated() does not call set_config. When the setting exists, current_setting(name, false) returns the same text as current_setting(name, true). current_setting is STABLE, so the planner never evaluates the THEN branch early; the harness confirms this, since the fresh-connection test (setting absent) calls current_actor() and passes under the mutant. Every input and state gives the same result with no error.
platform.transition_signature_check#3: 0910:29, the default of `coalesce(pg_catalog.pg_input_is_valid(p_aggregate_id, 'uuid'), false)` becomes `true`. pg_input_is_valid is STRICT and its second argument is the constant 'uuid', so the default is used only when p_aggregate_id is NULL; for every non-NULL id both versions take the same branch. For a NULL id the original returns NULL at line 30. The mutant goes on to `select * into v_state from platform.aggregate_state where aggregate_type = p_aggregate_type and aggregate_id = p_aggregate_id::uuid`: casting NULL raises nothing, `aggregate_id = NULL` is never true, and SELECT INTO without STRICT raises nothing when no row is found, so `not found` holds and it returns NULL at line 34. That select only reads (no FOR UPDATE, no side effect). Both return NULL for every input and state. (The state engine never passes NULL: platform.verify_signature receives p_aggregate_id::text of the uuid whose state row platform.transition has just locked.) Checked with the harness: no test of the group detects it.
platform.transition_signature_check#21: 0910:42, `v_signed < v_entered` becomes `v_signed <= v_entered`. The two differ only when both are non-NULL and equal: when either is NULL, the terms `v_entered is null or v_signed is null` before it are already true in both. v_signed is min(e.id) over kernel.audit_event rows with table_name = 'esig.signature' (0910:40-41); v_entered is max(e.id) over rows joined on e.table_name = 'platform.state_history' (0910:36-39). Each value is the id of a row, a row has one table_name, so the two come from different rows, and kernel.audit_event.id is the primary key (0010: `id bigint generated always as identity primary key`). They are never equal, for any input or state. Checked with the harness: no test of the group detects it.
